 Navigation Toggle Bryce McGowens #11 of the New Orleans Pelicans passes the ball Monday at Golden State. ( Noah Graham ) Warriors 138, Pelicans 87: Derik Queen 16 points | Postgame wrap
 Warriors (8-3), Pelicans (4-7); NOLA vs. Nets on Wednesday
 Jim Eichenhofer November 9, 2026 11:28 PM CST It was going to be a difficult task for New Orleans to slow down one of the NBA’s hottest teams – and that was before the Pelicans’ starting forwards were ruled out of action. With Trey Murphy (knee) and Zion Williamson (rest) not in uniform, Golden State rapidly seized control, leading by 30-plus points in the first half Monday, then expanding that edge to 50 early in the fourth quarter. It was the Warriors’ eighth consecutive victory after starting the season 0-3.
 New Orleans was frigid shooting-wise from the jump (finished at 36 percent on field goals, 29 percent on threes) and couldn’t get stops defensively, allowing Golden State to drain three-pointers and generate easy buckets off backcuts and ball movement in halfcourt offense. The Warriors scored at least 35 points in each of the first three periods.
 BY THE NUMBERS 
 21/44: Golden State three-point shooting. With New Orleans going 8/28 from long range, the hosts scored 39 more points just from triples.
 50-31: Warriors rebounding advantage. Herb Jones and Karlo Matkovic led the Pelicans with six boards apiece.
 NEXT FOR NEW ORLEANS 
 A five-game homestand tips off Wednesday vs. Brooklyn (7 p.m.), the only guest among the handful of opponents that currently has a losing record (the other visitors are Memphis, Denver, Golden State and Detroit). The Pelicans have won three of their last four games in the Smoothie King Center, with victories against Sacramento, Atlanta and Utah, followed by Friday’s loss to Minnesota.
 NEXT VS. WARRIORS 
 In exactly one week, Golden State will pay a visit to New Orleans on Nov. 16. That will be the last Pelicans-Warriors meeting until just prior to the All-Star break in February.
